title: Zoo Animals
story: The local zoo needs a digital animal catalog. Lions have an age. Elephants have an age AND weight. Penguins have a name (the zookeepers name each one). You need one type that describes all three, then functions to check which ones are babies.
why: Enum variants can have completely different fields � each animal type carries only what's relevant to it.
analogy: Animals are like different ID cards. A Lion card has an age field. An Elephant card has age AND weight. A Penguin card doesn't have age at all � it has a name. The zoo zookeeper reads each card differently.
try_it: Add a `Giraffe(height: Float64, age: Int)` variant. Update `describe` to mention height in meters. Update `is_baby` and `total_age` to handle Giraffe. Create a baby giraffe (0.5m, age 1) and an adult giraffe (5.5m, age 7).
tips: Use `_` to ignore fields you don't need in a match arm: `Elephant(age, _)` ignores weight
Different variants can have different numbers of fields � the compiler tracks this for you
Name variants after the thing they represent: `Lion`, not `LionAnimal` � the enum name provides context
common_mistakes: Trying to access `age` on a Penguin � penguins don't have an age field in this model
Forgetting the `_` wildcard on unused fields � match arms must bind or ignore every field
